title: Teacher guide: My path
intro: This guide supports using My path with young people (17–20) in adult basic education. The game is a tool for discussion and practice, not a test and not a substitute for a guidance conversation. Timings are suggestions.

ul: Fifteen checkpoints on a future map. Each has a situation, three options, an own option and the possibility to ask for another situation.
After a choice come reflection on consequences and a task. A star is given when the task (or the alternative task) is done. It is not tied to a particular choice and is never lost.
Every situation is about the story’s young person. Nobody has to tell about their own life.
Play it yourself. One checkpoint takes about 5–10 minutes; the whole game is too much for one lesson.
Choose the checkpoints for your group: tick them in Settings, or use a link with ?only=r01,r02,r03.
Prepare a support list (teacher, study counsellor, student welfare, support persons) and display it before checkpoint 5.
Check: texts and information were written with AI help. Have a native Finnish speaker review them and adapt them to your own education system.
Go through the safety rules on the start screen together before playing.
Emergency (life or health at risk): call 112. In the game an emergency call is only practised verbally; nobody dials.
The game asks for no names and stores no free text. Do not ask students to write private matters anywhere.
5 min: safety rules and explanation.
25–35 min: in pairs, 2–3 checkpoints. Read the situation, choose an option, discuss consequences and do the task.
10–15 min: shared debrief and the personal future map (final screen).
Every task has language support: a key word and a ready sentence. Words can be tapped.
Do not correct language errors while playing. Note useful expressions and return to them at the end.
Differentiation: stronger readers read in roles, others use the word help and larger text size.
Checkpoints 4 (family conflict), 5 (difficulties), 6 (pressure, substances, violence), 10 (prejudice), 12 (scam), 13 (responsibility at home) carry a content note. Nobody is forced.
Do not act out substance use or violence. Practise refusing, leaving and asking for help. Do not repeat racist expressions.
Checkpoint 15 (moving abroad): the game does not settle permit or residence matters. Those are checked individually.
Checkpoint 12: use no real account details. If credentials may have been compromised, contact the bank and report to the police.
If a student shares something worrying, follow your institution’s procedures and offer a private conversation.
A star = a practised skill. It is not a grade or a means of comparison.
A student may skip a situation or task or ask for another. The alternative task gives the same chance of a star.
A checkpoint can be revisited to try another option.
Which choice was hardest? What did the consequence teach?
Who could help the story’s young person? How is help asked for?
What is one small next step? (final screen; answers are written on paper or said aloud)
The photos show Keuda premises. Check image rights before publishing.
Progress is stored in the browser. On a shared device use “Delete saved progress” in Settings.
